part.name: Reinforced four-point clevis mounting bracket
part.description: Single-piece bracket with four end mounting holes, a raised central two-ear clevis joint, sloping load-distribution shells, and a recessed ribbed underside cavity. The STEP model is one solid with 266 B-rep faces and approximate overall dimensions 13.28 x 4.92 x 8.25 mm.
part.symmetry_note: The layout is approximately bilateral about the longitudinal center plane through the clevis gap, particularly at the two clevis ears. The two-hole mounting groups occur at both longitudinal ends, but the outer shell, underside cavity, blends, and local edge details are not exactly end-to-end symmetric.

Section.name: Main load-bearing shell
Section.function intent: Connect the two end mounting regions to the central clevis while spreading joint and mounting loads over a broad, stiff body.
Section.physical behavior: The broad plate carries membrane tension and compression, while the raised and curved shell surfaces increase section depth and bending stiffness. The sloping wings redirect concentrated clevis loads toward the four mounting points and reduce abrupt stress changes.
Section.geometry: A long, irregular plate-like shell with a substantially planar underside, two large sloping side facets, curved upper wing patches, and a raised central bridge. Its plan outline narrows near the middle and expands into paired lobes at both ends.
Section.location: Extends over the full part length between the left and right mounting groups and surrounds the central clevis support.

Section.name: Left mounting group
Section.function intent: Provide two separated fastener locations for attaching one end of the bracket to a mating frame or plate.
Section.physical behavior: The through holes locate and constrain fasteners, while the annular lands accept clamp force. Thick surrounding lobes resist bearing and tear-out, and the curved transitions spread bolt loads into the main shell.
Section.geometry: A paired-lobe mounting end with two circular holes passing through the local plate thickness. Each hole is surrounded by a raised or clearly bounded annular land and a rounded outer perimeter.
Section.location: At the low-x longitudinal end of the STEP model; this corresponds to one paired mounting end visible at the top or bottom of the plan views.

major_faces.name: Left paired-lobe perimeter

Section.name: Right mounting group
Section.function intent: Provide the second pair of fastener locations and establish a wide four-point attachment footprint for the bracket.
Section.physical behavior: The separated holes resist translation and rotation of the bracket on its support. The rounded lobe walls carry fastener bearing loads, and the surrounding shell transitions distribute clamp and service loads into the central body.
Section.geometry: A paired rounded mounting end containing two circular through holes with planar seating lands. The exterior is formed from several intersecting cylindrical and blended patches.
Section.location: At the high-x longitudinal end of the STEP model, opposite the left mounting group.

Section.name: Central clevis joint
Section.function intent: Receive a mating link between two ears and support a transverse pivot pin or joint fastener.
Section.physical behavior: The coaxial bores constrain the pin axis while allowing rotation of a mating link about that axis. The two separated ears react pin shear and bearing loads, and their wide inclined roots transfer those loads into the shell with reduced bending concentration.
Section.geometry: Two parallel plate-like ears rise from the middle of the bracket. Each ear has a large transverse cylindrical bore and a rounded crown. A rectangular gap between the ears provides clearance for a mating linkage.
Section.location: Raised above the longitudinal middle of the part, between the four end mounting points.

Section.name: Underside cavity and reinforcement
Section.function intent: Increase bending and torsional stiffness without filling the entire bracket volume, while preserving clearance and reducing mass.
Section.physical behavior: The ribs act as webs that carry shear between the upper shell and lower plate. The recessed cavity removes low-stress material, while the longitudinal and diagonal members stabilize the broad shell surfaces against local bending and buckling.
Section.geometry: A large underside recess bounded by inclined planar walls and a shallow curved roof. Several narrow cylindrical or blended rib-root bands follow diagonal and longitudinal load paths, forming a truss-like internal reinforcement pattern.
Section.location: On the underside of the central body, below and to both sides of the clevis root.
